title: YZ lithium niobate thickness-extension resonator: admittance and BVD fit (analytic, frequency response)
description:
A 100 um long, 5 um wide bar of YZ lithium niobate (crystal entry, euler 0, 90, 90: model x = crystal Z, the c_ij, piezo_e* and eps_dc* of the crystal data), 40 x 2 cells of 2.5 um, plane strain, piezoelectric: clamped (fixed) and grounded at x_lo, free with the drive electrode (1 V) at x_hi, rollers on y_lo / y_hi (uniaxial strain, y-uniform fields: the exact 1D thickness-extension problem along crystal Z with c = c33, e = e33, eps = eps33^S). Losses: mechanical_loss_factor 1e-3 (Q ~ 1000), dielectric_loss_tangent 1e-3. Study frequency_response: 481 frequencies over 17.6-18.8 MHz around mode 1.
Analytic (continuum, lossless): Z = (h / (j omega eps W)) (1 - K_t^2 tan(k h) / (k h)) per m of depth, k = omega / v_D, v_D = sqrt(c_D / rho), c_D = c + e^2 / eps, K_t^2 = e^2 / (eps c_D) = 0.026: antiresonance f_a = v_D / (4 h) = 18.29 MHz, resonance tan x = x / K_t^2 at x = pi / 2 - delta (delta from the quadratic of cot delta = 1 / delta - delta / 3, error ~1e-9), f_r = 18.10 MHz, k_eff^2 = 1 - (f_r / f_a)^2 = 0.0213, clamped capacitance C0 = eps W / h = 1.28e-11 F/m.
Derived values tab: the admittance feature's Butterworth-Van Dyke fit bvd_f_s / bvd_f_p against f_r / f_a (Q1 with 40 elements is ~6e-5 high, the single-mode BVD of a distributed resonator adds ~1e-4), k_eff2 (~1e-2), C0 (the fitted C0 also holds the static share of the higher modes, ~K_t^2 (1 - 8 / pi^2) = 0.5 %), Q_s ~ 1 / mechanical_loss_factor. Curves tab: admittance abs (|Y| in S/m) with bvd_abs (the fitted circuit) over it; phase. Snapshot slider: one snapshot per frequency (real part of the response, u_abs = |u|). The material constants below repeat the crystal data of materials/crystal_tensors.py (lithium_niobate: c33 2.45e11 Pa, e33 1.3 C/m^2, eps33^S 29, rho 4700, transcribed from memory: verify against Kovacs 1990 before trusting the absolute values).
